roads.name: Chemin Lucien-Lefrançois
words: Sweeping and steady: 12 curves in 3.2 miles.
Tight and technical: most curves turn on a radius under 130 ft.
From 392 to 708 ft, with 502 ft of up and down along the way.
Wooded nearly the whole way.
Homes line much of it: about 49 buildings a mile beside the road.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 70 km/h limit its corners still ask for about 1.69 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace.
